speedrun: List the repository, protocol, Cargo workspace, fixtures, binary, shared library, and helper executable.
Read the protocol documentation and relevant Rust modules for stdin/stdout handling, journal records, checkpoints, recovery, deduplication, windows, and histogram aggregation.
Build the workspace and run the existing tests or smoke command.
Run metricq against the visible fixture and capture protocol responses, logs, metrics, and recovery behavior.
Inspect the histogram wrapper and ABI header; run histprobe on singleton values, weights, quantiles, boundary values, and merges.
Create a small differential script comparing uninterrupted execution with checkpoint/recover execution.
Use that script to isolate the record replay at the saved journal offset and the retry/out-of-order identity failures.
Inspect journal offset advancement and checkpoint serialization code.
Inspect recovery parsing and distinguish incomplete final lines from malformed complete records.
Inspect event identity tracking and replace any per-stream maximum-sequence logic with durable event-identity tracking.
Ensure identity handling occurs before lateness filtering and is restored from checkpoints or replay state.
Fix the checkpoint offset to represent the first uncommitted journal record.
Make recovery ignore only a truncated final record while preserving existing errors for complete invalid requests.
Ensure live and recovered aggregation both use the opaque histogram wrapper, including weighted adds and merges.
Implement or repair half-open event-time windows and the configured lateness cutoff consistently across all paths.
Build and run targeted retry, out-of-order, late-event, duplicate, multi-stream, and empty-window cases.
Run checkpoint/recovery equivalence and repeated-recovery idempotence tests.
Run the full protocol matrix, generated workload, and metrics/log consistency checks; verify stdout contains only responses.
Inspect the final diff and rebuild from a clean state.
invalid_failure_risks: The opaque helper may not provide enough information to uniquely infer percentile bucket boundaries and merge behavior for arbitrary hidden inputs; requiring exact semantics beyond what can be experimentally identified would be underdetermined.

The statement that valid late events must not disappear conflicts with a configured lateness policy that may intentionally drop events; the allowed behavior at and beyond the cutoff should be specified precisely.

It is unclear whether malformed complete journal records should be skipped, reported, or fail recovery, versus only malformed final records being tolerated; tests must define this distinction exactly.
Stable JSON field ordering is not normally a JSON protocol property, so exact textual ordering should be specified separately from semantic response equality.
The build claim depends on all pinned Rust crates and native dependencies already being cached in the image; otherwise the no-network requirement makes the task invalid.

Checkpoint format and whether deduplication state must be serialized directly or may be reconstructed by replay are not fully specified, which could make otherwise equivalent implementations fail implementation-specific tests.
review.reasons: The task has a realistic interacting recovery/deduplication defect and a meaningful opaque-component investigation, while the protocol and verification plan are detailed enough to support deterministic outcome testing. It is challenging but plausibly solvable in the stated container, although the speedrun is near the practical limit for an hour and several edge semantics need tighter specification.
fixes: Define the lateness rule mathematically, including whether late events are intentionally dropped and the exact inclusive or exclusive cutoff behavior.
Document the required behavior for malformed complete journal records separately from an incomplete final line, including whether recovery continues and what is logged.
State the checkpoint contract explicitly: the meaning of the saved offset, required durable identity state, and whether recovery must tolerate repeated invocation without writing duplicate records.
Add a finite characterization contract or reference probe corpus for the opaque histogram so hidden tests do not require information that histprobe cannot identify.
Clarify whether stable field ordering is asserted byte-for-byte or only required for the service's canonical serializer.
Ensure the Dockerfile includes or vendors every Rust dependency and native build prerequisite needed for an offline clean build.

verdicts.reason: Although both involve deterministic journal recovery and idempotent replay, this task centers on event-time rolling weighted-percentile computation and lateness handling rather than reconstructing a transactional multi-tenant object store.

Both process timestamped events and use half-open time semantics, but this task repairs percentile windows with checkpointed journal recovery instead of campaign sessions, attribution, purchases, and refunds.

Both query metrics using a compiled implementation, but this task requires stateful event ingestion, checkpoint/recovery, deduplication, lateness policy, and weighted percentiles rather than an HTTP read-only aggregation service.
This task has no shared central problem with incident archival, alias resolution, correlation components, or dependency ordering beyond generic deterministic event processing.
This task concerns rolling metric computation and durable replay, whereas the reference validates authenticated audit chains and emits checkpointed events.
